title: Sequence & branching in C#
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: Why would Unicode be chosen instead of standard ASCII for a multilingual application?

blocks.title: Sequence = instructions in order
blocks.text: Sequence is the normal top-to-bottom execution of statements. Each statement happens after the previous one unless another construct changes the flow.

blocks.title: Input arrives as text
blocks.text: Console.ReadLine() returns a string. If the program needs a whole number, parse the input into an int .

blocks.title: Branching chooses a route
blocks.text: An if condition must evaluate to true or false . Only the matching branch is executed.

blocks.title: Conditions and order matter
blocks.text: Use == to compare equality, not = . Use && , || and ! for AND, OR and NOT. With else if , conditions are tested from top to bottom. Put the most demanding threshold first.

blocks.title: Even or odd
blocks.text: Ask for a whole number. Output Even when the remainder after division by 2 is zero; otherwise output Odd .

blocks.title: Build the missing decision
blocks.text: Console.Write("Number: "); int number = int.Parse(Console.ReadLine()); if (number % 2 == 0) { Console.WriteLine("Even"); } else { Console.WriteLine("Odd"); } C# % is the remainder operator; it matches OCR MOD .
